why: This is the classic task-scheduler problem: regions are task types and minGap is the cooldown. The most frequent region forces (maxFreq-1) blocks of width minGap+1 plus a final partial block holding every region tied for the max, and the total can never be less than n.
hints: Only the counts per region matter, not the order of the string. Which region is hardest to place?
Lay out the most frequent region first: copies separated by minGap gaps. That skeleton has (maxFreq - 1) * (minGap + 1) slots before the last copy, and every other region fits into the gaps.
Answer = max(n, (maxFreq - 1) * (minGap + 1) + number of regions with count maxFreq). O(n) with a counter.
pitfalls: If there are more requests than gap slots, no idle time is needed and the answer is just n.
All regions tied at the maximum frequency go in the final block, not just one.
minGap = 0 means any order works: answer n.
constraints:
• Not stated in the source; the same task in the bank (getMinTime2) uses:
  • 1 ≤ requests.length ≤ 10^5, lowercase letters
  • 0 ≤ minGap ≤ 100
